newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts down, off lows aided by long end buying.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts down, off lows aided by long end buying.

text.p: UK gilts futures were down but comfortably above their early lows after some mild buying interest at the long and medium end.
"We've seen some buying of the longs and a bit of the shorts but overall it's still very quiet. The (U.S.) Treasury market is really telling us where to go," one gilt dealer at a UK brokerage said.
U.S. Treasuries fell back sharply on Friday after stronger than expected employment data and a rise in the NAPM and remained weak this morning.

The UK has little to go on on the domestic front today and brushed aside an unexpected slowdown in July narrow money supply growth to 5.9 percent from a revised 6.2 percent in June. The measure remains above the official zero to four percent monitoring range but analysts say it is unlikely to be a cause of concern.
By 0910 GMT, LIFFE September gilts were down 4/32 at 114-25/32, compared with the session's low of 114-18/32 whilst Bunds were 15 basis points slimmer at 102.32.
"Gilts are just in no man's land at the moment, no-one wants to play," said another trader.
"The market's worried about how high sterling is, the consensus is that it's unsustainable but no-one is brave enough to sell it," he said.
The gilt/Bund spread widened back out to 153, having come in to 147 on Friday. Dealers say there is good support at 158-160 basis points.

There is speculation that German rates will rise this week as the Bundesbank tries to support the ailing deutschemark. The central bank is due to announce the repo rate for the next two weeks on Tuesday with the results of the repo out on Wednesday.

The other international focus is the U.S. refunding auctions, with the Treasury set to auction $16.0 billion in three-year notes on Tuesday, $12.0 billion of 10-year notes on Wednesday and then $10.0 billion of 30-year bonds the following week.
The possibility of a rate change is dominating the UK agenda. The Bank of England's Monetary Policy Committee meets on Wednesday and Thursday with the result due the second day.
A Reuter poll found 16 out of 23 London economists expect British official rate to rise to 7.0 percent from 6.75 percent this week, although most say the decision is finely balanced.
At the short end of the yield curve, LIFFE September short sterling was unchanged at 92.68, discounting base rates of 7.25 percent.
